current_inference.orientation: Direct reorientation studies now span natural downward, horizontal and down-slope optima. The general working hypothesis is therefore not that downward orientation is universally superior, but that locally integrated natural orientation can increase fitness through different combinations of pollinator presentation/filtering and abiotic protection. The two-study homologous seed/achene-set lnRR diagnostic has high heterogeneity, reinforcing context dependence.
current_inference.stickiness: A universal sticky-is-defence rule is not retained. Direct floral evidence includes strong benefit in Bejaria and a Cirsium null elsewhere in the repository, while whole-plant Datura shows substantial costs; context-dependent defence is the working hypothesis.
current_inference.display: Direct manipulation supports simultaneous pollinator-attraction benefit and seed-predator cost, but broad-angiosperm numerical common-effect extraction is incomplete.
current_inference.bract_defence: Pedicularis rex directly separates pathways: draining water-holding bracts left pollinator visitation unchanged but increased seed predation and reduced final seed set. This supports a defence/protection mechanism rather than generic pollinator attraction.
current_inference.colour_pigmentation: UV experiments support both an environmental selection-pressure axis and a plausible anthocyanin UV-screening mechanism. However, intact-flower pigment-causal reproductive fitness evidence remains insufficient; colder/darker or UV/darker adaptive claims remain hypotheses.
